title: Why a MOSFET Never Completely Turns Off

segments.text: What happens when the gate voltage falls below threshold?
The MOSFET enters cutoff, where ideally no drain‑source current flows.
In reality, thermal energy lets a few electrons hop over the barrier, creating a tiny exponential subthreshold current described by ID ≈ ID0 e^(VGS−Vth)/nVT.
This leakage is like a leaky faucet—you can’t shut it off completely, a drip remains.
Engineers sometimes exploit this weak‑inversion region for ultra‑low‑power circuits.
The subthreshold current follows an exponential rule, making it measurable even when the switch seems off.
So that gate voltage below threshold still allows a whisper of current.
